invariants.text: An order item's order_id must reference an existing order in the Order entity.
An order item's product_id must reference an existing product in the Product entity.
Each order can contain multiple order items, each representing a different quantity or unit price of the same or different products.
Each product can appear in multiple orders through order items.
Order.created_at must be a datetime
Order.created_at must not be null
Order.order_id must be an auto-incremented integer primary key with default value None
Order.updated_at must be a datetime
Order.updated_at must not be null
OrderItem.order_id must be an integer
OrderItem.order_id must not be null
OrderItem.order_id must reference an existing Order.order_id
OrderItem.order_item_id must be an auto-incremented integer primary key with default value None
OrderItem.product_id must be an integer
OrderItem.product_id must not be null
OrderItem.product_id must reference an existing Product.product_id
OrderItem.quantity must be an integer
OrderItem.quantity must not be null
OrderItem.unit_price must be a number
OrderItem.unit_price must not be null
Product.description must be a string
Product.name must be a string
Product.name must not be null
Product.product_id must be an auto-incremented integer primary key with default value None
The order total amount is calculated as the sum of (quantity * unit_price) across all order items in the order.
The quantity in an order item must be greater than zero.
The total order amount must equal the sum of the quantity multiplied by unit price for each order item in the order.
The unit price in an order item must be greater than zero.
When a product is removed from an order, the order total amount must be recalculated based on the remaining items.
When an order item is deleted, the order total amount must be recalculated based on the remaining items.
